text_beyond_claims: - Sentence {sentence} says more than its claims: a reader takes it to state `{claim}`, which is {value}{why}. Evidence: {evidence}. {advice} Change the sentence itself, not only its claims.
format_error: - {error}. This is not a valid DSL line; use only the forms in the DSL reference.
missing_term: - The text does not mention {names}, one of the model's most important terms. Add a sentence about it, with its claims.
emphasis: - Sentence {sentence} opens the text with {minor}, a minor part of the model's importance, and names none of its strongest drivers ({strong}). Open with the most important drivers; mention minor ones later.
false: The facts contradict it. Change the statement to what the facts show, or drop it.
insufficient_evidence: The data do not settle it at this sample size. State it as a set of values, hedge it with unsettled(...), or drop it.
unknown_term: The model has no such term. Use only the features named in the facts.
not_applicable: This kind of claim does not apply to that term.
strength: Its share of the importance is {share} (95% band {low} to {high}), which spans {classes}. A strength word fits only if the whole band lies within the classes it names.
strength_undetected: A word for an effect (weak, moderate, strong) also needs an effect the data detect, and they detect none.
share: Its share of the importance is {share} (95% band {low} to {high}). "About {claimed}" fits only if the whole band lies within {fit_low} to {fit_high}.
rank: Its rank is {rank} (95% band {low} to {high}). A single rank fits only if the band is that one rank; otherwise name the ranks the band spans.
no_jump: The curve has no single sharp step the data confirm: its largest step, near {at}, {why}. No location makes "jumps at" true, and hedging the location does not help; describe the rise with a direction, and leave out the step and its location.
no_jump_small: is at most {ratio} of the curve's range, and a jump needs at least half
jump_elsewhere: The largest jump lies near {at} (95% band {low} to {high}). Name a location in that band.
no_peak: The curve has no peak inside its range: its highest part is not clearly above both sides. No location makes "peaks at" true, and hedging the location does not help; describe the shape with a direction, and leave out the peak.
peak_elsewhere: The highest part of the curve lies at {low} to {high}. Name a location there.
hedge_settled_true: The data settle this: the claim inside the hedge is true. State it instead of hedging it.
hedge_settled_false: The data settle this: the claim inside the hedge is false. State what the facts show instead of hedging it.
unexpressed: - Sentence {sentence} states a number that no claim form can check: {statements}. Say it in a form the DSL reference has, with its claim, or leave the number out.
missing_in_text: - The text does not state anything about {names} that a reader can find, although it is one of the model's most important terms: your claims about it are not in the sentences. Say it in a sentence, with its claims.
